newsitem.title: UK: IEA admits 1996 oil forecasts missed target.
newsitem.headline: IEA admits 1996 oil forecasts missed target.

text.p: The International Energy Agency (IEA) on Friday admitted its forecasts for 1996 world oil supply and demand proved wide of the mark because of unforeseen events and shortcomings in its methodology.

The biggest correction was to the Paris-based agency's forecast for supply from producers outside the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), which was slashed by 650,000 barrels per day (bpd), equivalent to the production of a country like Colombia.
Almost as significant was the OECD energy watchdog's underestimate of demand in 1996, which was subject to an upward revision of 310,000 bpd since its Monthly Oil Market report last March.
Together the changes imply an extra 960,000 bpd of demand.
Oil prices hit a six-year high of $25.06 a barrel in October last year against a background of strong demand, slower than expected supply growth and low stocks.

The IEA said its forecasts are supposed to represent what the supply-demand balance would look like given "normal" events, but it conceded making "misjudgements of the underlying supply trends that drove the market in 1996".
